title: Access Controls Evidence Roadmap for Auditors
content:
Purpose:
This briefing is intended as an auditor-facing roadmap that bundles control mappings, a concise gap analysis, and a Q&A shell for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 assessments focusing on access control (RBAC v2), audit log schema, SIEM exportability, and evidence automation. It is written to speed evidence collection and reduce back-and-forth during evidence requests.

Scope:
- Controls: access provisioning/deprovisioning, privilege management, role design, authentication/authorization events, audit-log completeness and integrity, log export and retention, and automated evidence pipelines.
- Systems in scope: Redwood Console (identity + role management UI), Serving runtime auth hooks, Private/VPC control plane, Audit-log ingestion service, SIEM export pipeline (Kafka -> ES/Logstash), evidence automation service (internal).

Executive summary / high-level findings:
- RBAC v2 provides role templates, inheritance, and attribute-based binding to service principals. Most role definitions and assignment history are already auditable via the role-change events stream.
- Audit log schema covers core authentication and authorization events (login, token issuance, role-grant, role-revoke, API key rotation, model access). However, several event attributes (actor_ip, request_id propagation across services, and pre/post policy snapshot) are inconsistently populated for cross-region failover flows.
- SIEM export exists and is configured for parity to retention policy, but some exported fields are transformed and mapped under different keys which complicates automated evidence ingestion.
- Evidence automation (playbooks + runbooks) exists for routine user access reviews and on-demand auditor bundles, but end-to-end coverage for Private deployments is partial.

Control mapping (summary):
- SOC 2: CC6 (Logical and physical access controls) / CC7 (System operations) -> Redwood controls: RBAC v2 role lifecycle, privileged role review cadence, authentication log capture, time-based session revocation.
- ISO 27001: A.9 (Access control) -> RBAC role definitions, unique IDs for identities, principle of least privilege demonstrated via role templates and runtime enforcement.
- Evidence sources mapped to control objectives:
  - Role definitions + templates: Confluence design doc + role manifest files (git) + Console export
  - Role assignment history: role-change event stream (audit-log), archived CSV snapshots produced by evidence automation
  - Privileged access approvals: Signed tickets (JIRA SEC-PRIV) + Approval comment threads + PRs for temporary elevation automation
  - Authentication & authorization events: auth-service logs (timestamp, user_id, method, result) -> SIEM export
  - Token and key lifecycle: key-rotation logs + KMS audit events

Gap analysis (top items):
1) Missing actor_ip in certain cross-region proxy events (severity: medium)
   - Impact: reduces ability to correlate suspicious logons to origin.
   - Recommended fix: propagate and persist X-Forwarded-For from edge, add explicit actor_ip field to cross-region event enrichment job.
   - Evidence to attach: proposed PR, enrichment job runbook, reprocessed sample logs.

2) Inconsistent request_id across microservices during failover (severity: high)
   - Impact: impedes end-to-end request tracing for authorization decisions and forensics.
   - Recommended fix: make request_id mandatory for internal RPCs, enforce in service mesh sidecar, add a small retroactive stitching tool for recent window.
   - Evidence to attach: RFC, Jira task, sidecar config diff, test logs showing request_id present.

3) SIEM export field-mapping mismatch for role_change.reason and role_change.policy_snapshot (severity: low)
   - Impact: automation that produces auditor bundles may miss textual approval context.
   - Recommended fix: add canonical fields to export schema and a migration job to copy legacy fields.
   - Evidence to attach: mapping table, ETL job PR, sample exported JSON.

4) Private deployments: partial automation of evidence collection (severity: medium-high)
   - Impact: manual evidence collection for on-prem customers increases auditor friction and time to close.
   - Recommended fix: ship a small evidence-collector agent and documented runbook for customers to run that produces a signed evidence bundle.
   - Evidence to attach: design spec, customer-runbook draft, sample bundle.

Recommended evidence checklist for auditor bundle (what to include on first request):
- Executive summary (1 page) mapping requested control to Redwood artifact names and owners.
- Role manifest snapshot (JSON/CSV) and a diff showing change during the period under review.
- Role assignment audit-log export (CSV) with columns: timestamp, actor_id, target_principal, role_id, action, justification_id, request_id.
- Authentication and authorization logs covering the review period exported from SIEM (NDJSON or CSV) with the recommended minimal fields: timestamp, service, event_type, user_id, actor_ip, request_id, result, policy_snapshot_id.
- Privileged access approvals: links to approval tickets and redacted copies of approvals where needed.
- Key rotation evidence: KMS audit logs with rotation events and associated ticket ids.
- Evidence automation run: log showing run start/end, inputs, produced bundle checksum and storage location + signature.
- Data retention policy excerpt and SIEM retention confirmation for the period.

SIEM export schema - recommended minimal fields (auditor-friendly):
- ts (ISO8601), service, env, event_type, user_id, actor_type (human/service), actor_email, actor_ip, request_id, trace_id, session_id, auth_method, outcome, resource_type, resource_id, role_id, policy_snapshot_id, justification_id, raw_payload_url
- Retention policy: 13 months hot, 24 months cold archival (policy excerpt attached).

Audit Q&A (prepared answers and pointers to evidence)
Q: How do you prove role assignments were approved?
A: We link role assignment events to approval tickets via justification_id. Evidence bundle includes the CSV of role_change events plus the JIRA ticket links and, where required, a redacted approval record. See artifacts: role-change-2024Q3.csv, JIRA-PRIV-197.

Q: Can you show an example of a failed authorization and how it was investigated?
A: Yes — provide auth-service logs for the incident (auth-fail-2024-07-11.ndjson), the SIEM alert ticket, the incident postmortem, and correlating request traces using request_id to map the flow across services.

Q: How do you ensure completeness of logs across multi-region deployments?
A: We enforce event publication to a central audit topic (Kafka cluster) before final acknowledgement. For cross-region failover we currently buffer and replicate events; the work-item to ensure actor_ip + request_id propagation is tracked in JIRA-SEC-482. Attach: Kafka topic policy, producer config.

Q: How do you demonstrate deletion/deprovision events for an employee?
A: Evidence bundle includes: deprovision ticket, role-change event (revoke), access token invalidation event, and subsequent failed auth attempts (if any). We provide a timeline CSV and signed bundle.

Packaging and automation notes (how to produce the bundle quickly):
1) Evidence automation job 'auditor-bundle' accepts a time window + customer id flag. It runs three steps in sequence: collect (SIEM query + audit topic pull), normalize (apply canonical schema mapping), sign & store (S3 + metadata in evidence-db).
2) For hosted accounts the job is fully automated and produces a single pre-signed tar.gz. For Private accounts the job can be run as a containerized agent that outputs an equivalent bundle.
3) Known manual steps: redaction of customer PII and approval ticket exports for certain privacy cases.

Action plan (owners + short timeline):
- Short-term (2–4 weeks): add actor_ip propagation to cross-region enrichment job (owner: Lucas Meyer). Add canonical export fields for role_change.reason (owner: Priya Nair).
- Mid-term (1–3 months): make request_id enforcement mandatory in service mesh sidecars and ship a retroactive stitching job (owner: Evan Cho).
- Mid-term (1–3 months): build a Private deployment evidence-collector agent (owner: Platform Eng lead).
- Long-term (3–6 months): roll out evidence automation for on-prem customers and add auditor bundle self-serve in Console (owner: security-and-compliance + product).

Appendix - quick reference artifacts to attach to initial auditor package:
- role-manifest-2024-09-01.json (git sha), role-change-2024Q3.csv, auth-logs-2024-09.ndjson, siem-export-mapping-v1.xlsx, JIRA-SEC-482, design-rfc-rbac-v2, evidence-automation-runbook-v0.7.pdf.

Notes and open questions (for internal follow-up):
- Confirm retention alignment for country-specific customers (EU data residency) and annotate bundles appropriately.
- Finalize canonical SIEM schema and publish a versioned mapping so automation doesn’t break on field renames.
- Validate agent packaging for on-prem so customers can run it without exposing secrets.

If auditors prefer, we can prepare a 30-minute walkthrough with screenshots of the Console exports, a live replay of the evidence automation job producing a bundle, and a short demo of request tracing across services for one sample request.
